chapter: Jamming, bootleg records and the Topsy hit
title: Hearing the edited 'Topsy' and its rise to number one
summary: He is unimpressed by the final edit at Jim and Andy's, but it climbs to number one.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: going to do, I think you got a number one hit. So anyway that night Gerry Mulligan, Hawk, Charlie Shavers and all of them went by the Metropole, I says come on with me, I said I want you to hear the record because in the Metropole we'd been playing the damn thing but it was like News, the Daily News, you know what the Metropole was like, behind the bar and we all reading and scuffling with it. So anyway Gerry Mulligan and all of us went up to Jim and Andy's, a place where all the musicians used to hang, Billie Butterfield, so we listened to it, and boy it sounded like shit to me, excuse me. Oh I didn't mean that.

It sounded like nothing to me, so I looked at Hawk and Gerry Mulligan and they said nice, Cozy. Well you know they don't want to bring me down and say, Cozy, that sound terrible, you know, but it sound just terrible to me, because I had another side that I was going to pick up, the A side or the B side, I just forget now. So, in a way I'm glad they did edit it like that it satisfied all these other tin ears out here that didn't know anything about music, and so before I knew it it was about 75 on the charts, the next couple of weeks, 40, then it got up there to be number 10, then it got to be number one and stayed number one. I says, ain't that something, and I didn't think anything of it at the beginning. It was number one for months.
